newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - U.S. drug companies' Q3 seen up 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - U.S. drug companies' Q3 seen up 14 pct.

text.p: A batch of new drugs combined with higher domestic sales volume and firm pricing will drive U.S. pharmaceutical companies' third-quarter earnings higher, despite the weight of a stronger dollar on overseas sales.
Industry analysts expect earnings per share for the group on average to rise about 14 percent, according to First Call.
Recently approved drugs carrying higher prices and heftier margins, compared with those on older medications, are beginning to bolster bottom lines, analysts said.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a "tide" of drugs in the past two years, said Rodman and Renshaw analyst James Keeney.
"It could be 70 new drugs by the end of the year that have higher prices and higher margins, on top of higher domestic growth for pharmaceuticals," Keeney said.
Recent high-profile approvals include American Home Products Corp's Redux for obesity, Merck and Co Inc's osteoporosis treatment Fosamax and Eli Lilly and Co's Zyprexa for schizophrenia.

The stronger dollar will clip about two percent on average from total third-quarter revenues, although currency hedging should soften the the blow on the bottom lines of drug companies, analysts said.
The strong dollar is "going to temper the top line, and to a certain extent the bottom line, in the second half," said Ken Kulju at UBS Securities.
